function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Key Points (2024)** | Topic | Summary | Practical Tips | |-------|---------|----------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits: 35–55 mph on rural roads, 45–65 mph on highways, 25–35 mph in residential zones.
• “No speed limit” roads (e.g., I‑10, I‑35) have a default 70 mph limit unless posted otherwise. | • Always obey posted signs; use a GPS that updates speed limit info. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat or booster.
• Texas law requires a child‑safety seat for children under 4 or 40 lb. | • Check the seat‑belt sign in your vehicle; use a rear‑view camera or mirror to confirm seat‑belt status. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02 %).
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, mandatory alcohol‑education programs, possible jail time. | • Use a designated driver or rideshare if you’ve had any alcohol. | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | • Install a hands‑free system or use voice‑activated controls. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has the right of way.
• Pedestrians always have priority at crosswalks. | • Yield to pedestrians and cyclists; use caution at school zones. | | **School Bus** | • Stop for a school bus with its stop sign extended and lights flashing.
• No passing on either side. | • Keep a safe distance; check for school‑bus signs. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals at least 100 ft before changing lanes.
• Do not exceed the posted speed limit when overtaking. | • Check mirrors and blind spots; signal early. | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a “no parking” zone can result in a ticket or towing. | • Look for parking meters or signs indicating restrictions. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display a valid registration sticker.
• Towing a vehicle requires a proper tow‑bar and a valid license. | • Keep registration documents in the glove compartment. | | **Insurance** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | • Verify coverage annually; consider higher limits for peace of mind. | | **Traffic Cameras & Speed Cameras** | • Speed cameras are used in many counties; fines are issued automatically. | • Drive within posted limits; avoid speeding in camera‑heavy areas. | | **Emergency Vehicles** | • Pull over to the right and stop when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. | • Do not block the intersection; stay out of the way. | | **Winter & Weather Conditions** | • Texas has mild winters, but sudden rain or ice can create hazardous conditions. | • Adjust speed and following distance; use headlights in low visibility. | ### Quick Reference Resources - **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official traffic laws, maps, and updates. - **Texas Motor Vehicle Commission (MVC)** – Licensing, registration, and insurance requirements. - **Texas Highway Patrol** – Enforcement and safety tips. ### Common Penalties (if applicable) | Offense | Typical Fine | Possible Additional Penalties | |---------|--------------|------------------------------| | Speeding (over 20 mph) | $100–$500 | License points, possible suspension | | DUI | $500–$2,000 | License suspension, mandatory education, jail | | Seat‑belt violation | $50–$200 | Points on license | | Cell‑phone use | $50–$200 | Points on license | **Tip:** Always keep a copy of the Texas Driver Handbook in your vehicle; it’s a handy reference for all traffic rules and regulations.
